questions: How many devices did you fabricate and cool down, and how many showed parity oscillations at the both-manifold sweet spot? The paper presents one device and two cooldowns (pp. 9, 24).
Why were the others set aside, if there were others?
Which ranges did you measure beyond those shown: parallel fields other than 150 mT, temperatures above base, coupler amplitudes above 11.25 mV, and other dot orbitals in the main cooldown?

What does the second-best dataset look like? Fig. ED9 was never checked in the odd manifold (p. 24); how many retunings in the main cooldown passed the both-manifold check, and what spread of (fodd - feven)/(fodd + feven) did they give?

Page 8 says the even–odd degeneracy "is protected against detuning of either QD individually", and page 9 says detuning a single QD "removes the sweet spot protection and suppresses the oscillations". Could you say which you mean, and quantify the splitting against single-dot detuning?
Fig. 3b bounds the product of the two chains' overlaps (p. 34). Do you have φ ≈ π data in both manifolds from the main cooldown that bound each chain on its own?
For the charge-qubit configuration in Fig. 4g,h, what is the shortest coherence time you could have resolved with 25 ns ramps, and so what does "no coherent oscillations are resolved" bound?

Fig. 2e was measured after a phase jump and a charge jump that left the device with "increased instability" (p. 24). How did you check each of the nine retunings, and were the crossings in both manifolds verified at each field?
